question: What is a TFSA?
expected_answer: A registered savings account where investment income (interest, dividends, capital gains) is generally tax-free, including when withdrawn.

question: Are TFSA contributions tax deductible?
expected_answer: No. Unlike RRSP contributions, TFSA contributions are not tax deductible.

question: Who is allowed to open a TFSA?
expected_answer: A Canadian resident who is at least 18 and has a valid social insurance number.

question: Can I put money back into my TFSA after I take some out?
expected_answer: Yes, but withdrawals are only added back to your contribution room at the start of the next calendar year, so re-contributing in the same year without room can cause an over-contribution.

question: When does money I withdraw from my TFSA get added back to my contribution room?
expected_answer: The withdrawn amount is added back to your contribution room on January 1 of the next calendar year.

question: What happens if I put too much money in my TFSA?
expected_answer: It is an over-contribution, taxed at 1% per month on the excess for as long as it stays in the account.

question: How is my TFSA contribution room calculated?
expected_answer: It is your annual TFSA dollar limit, plus any unused room from previous years, plus amounts withdrawn in the previous year.

question: Do TFSA withdrawals affect government benefits like the GST credit or Old Age Security?
expected_answer: No. TFSA income and withdrawals do not affect eligibility for federal income-tested benefits and credits such as OAS, GIS, EI, the Canada child benefit and the GST credit.

question: How do I move my TFSA from one bank to another without affecting my room?
expected_answer: Ask the receiving institution to do a direct transfer. A direct transfer between your own TFSAs does not affect your contribution room, but withdrawing and re-depositing yourself can.

question: Can I lose my TFSA's tax-free status by trading a lot?
expected_answer: Yes. If you trade with the frequency and experience of a professional trader, your TFSA may be deregistered and the income taxed as business income.

question: Are RRSP contributions tax deductible?
expected_answer: Yes. RRSP contributions can be deducted from your income, reducing the tax you pay.

question: Do I pay tax when I take money out of my RRSP?
expected_answer: Yes. You generally have to pay tax when you cash in or make withdrawals from an RRSP.

question: What do I have to do with my RRSP when I turn 71?
expected_answer: By the end of the year you turn 71 you must close the RRSP: withdraw it as cash (taxable), transfer it to a RRIF, or use it to buy an annuity.

question: How do I set up an RRSP?
expected_answer: Through a financial institution such as a bank, credit union, trust or insurance company.
